b: The investment provides fresh capital for the 127-year-old family business, which entered voluntary administration in Apr.
A.H. Beard will continue manufacturing mattresses in four Australian states following its recapitalisation (Image: Unsplash)

A.H. Beard has secured more than 200 jobs across four Australian states following its recapitalisation by Softide Investment, a subsidiary of Shanghai-listed smart bed and sleep technology manufacturer Keeson Technology Corporation.

Founded in 1899, A.H. Beard is Australia’s oldest mattress manufacturer. The fifth-generation family business produces mattresses in four states and supplies the residential, retail and hospitality markets.

The company entered voluntary administration in Apr 2026. Following a business turnaround led by administrator P.A. Lucas, the recapitalisation is expected to deliver significant returns to secured and unsecured creditors, while providing fresh capital to support its long-term operations.
CEO Matthew Beard will continue to lead the business alongside the Beard family and existing executive team.

A long-standing member of the Australian Furniture Association (AFA), A.H. Beard received support from the association and its members throughout the administration period. Several AFA members supply the company with materials and components, including foam, springs, textiles and timber, and continued working with the business during this time.
AFA group CEO Patrizia Torelli said the outcome had implications for the wider furniture supply chain, given the number of businesses dependent on A.H. Beard’s manufacturing operations.

“When a manufacturer of this size is in trouble, the effects reach a long way. Foam makers, spring and textile suppliers, timber fabricators and transport operators all plan their work around A.H. Beard’s production lines. The total ‘real’ job losses run into the thousands,” she said.

“Our members understood that. Many of them supply A.H. Beard, and they kept working with the business while its future was uncertain. That is what an industry network is for, and I’m proud of how our members responded,” she added.

Torelli said the AFA would continue working with the Beard family and the wider bedding sector on issues affecting local manufacturers, including government furniture procurement and product standards for mattresses sold in Australia.
Beard said the recapitalisation represented a vote of confidence in the company and Australian manufacturing.

“We’re immensely grateful to our customers, retail partners and suppliers who stood by us during this period. The support of the Australian Furniture Association and its members has meant a great deal to our team,” he said.
He added that the new capital and strategic partnership would support further investment in innovation and the company’s manufacturing operations.
